sub_questions: What forms does ontology drift take in the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base (additions, deprecations, revocations, sub-technique restructuring, tactic reassignment, silent description rewriting), and how large is each across the full public release history?
How stable are ATT&CK technique identifiers over time, and what is the survival/half-life profile of an identifier minted at release V when read at release W?
Do identifiers that remain valid nonetheless change meaning (silent semantic drift), and by how much?
What fraction of apparent growth in ATT&CK's adversary knowledge (group-to-technique edges) is genuine new intelligence versus ontology bookkeeping (sub-technique refinement, revocation re-mapping)?

How much accuracy does TTP-based threat-actor attribution lose when a CTI artefact written in release V's vocabulary is consumed by a knowledge base at release W, holding the underlying intelligence constant?
How much do detection/mitigation coverage claims change when the capability is frozen but the ontology moves?
How valid are the ATT&CK labels in real, widely used CTI corpora and benchmarks today, and can their authoring version be inferred when undeclared?
What normalization protocol restores cross-version comparability, how much of the damage does it repair, and where does it provably fail?
What reporting discipline should CTI papers, benchmarks and vendor claims adopt so results remain interpretable across ATT&CK releases?

How does this position against existing work on CTI quality, ATT&CK-based analytics, LLM CTI benchmarks, TTP extraction and attribution, and concept drift in security machine learning, and what must an SCI-level contribution here demonstrate?

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: primary artefacts first — the ATT&CK STIX release bundles themselves, benchmark label files and tool source cloned from public GitHub, and this run's own measurement outputs under data/results/, which are ground_truth tier. Peer-reviewed and arXiv literature is reachable only through the WebSearch tool in this environment, so secondary literature enters at summary fidelity and must be marked as such; never present a search summary as a verbatim quotation. Evidence norms: a measured number computed from the release corpus outranks any vendor or survey claim; a claim about a specific benchmark must be checked against that benchmark's own label file, not its paper. Recency: ATT&CK releases through v19.2 (August 2026) matter directly; CTI-benchmark literature from 2024 onward is the live comparison set.
